history.period: 15th century (attributed to King Kyamba, r. 1467-1508; attribution CONTESTED)
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 644 ('Vishnu Temple', Bishnupur — same temple). The 15th-century brick Vishnu Temple at Bishnupur (originally Lamangdong, 'the old capital', ~27 km southwest of Imphal) is one of Manipur's oldest Vaishnavite shrines and an ASI-protected monument. Tradition credits King Kyamba (Kiyamba, r. 1467-1508): after defeating the Shan kingdom of Kyang jointly with Khe-Khomba, king of Pong (Upper Burma), he is said to have received a Vishnu emblem/image from the Pong king and installed it here; the town was renamed Bishnupur ('abode of Vishnu') after the deity. Architecture is brick-and-lime masonry in the traditional Bengal-hut idiom with a corbelled roof, blending Bengali and Burmese styles; the sanctum is only about 2 m x 2 m. Scholarly caution: there is NO authentic record proving Kyamba built the temple — it was earlier Ngangom Phura, a shrine of the indigenous Meitei religion raised by the Ngangom clan, predating the Vishnu installation. In 2025 Rajya Sabha MP Sanajaoba raised a Zero Hour appeal for better ASI upkeep of the site. One recent visitor review reported the shrine closed with no idol inside (verify).

name: Bishnupur Vishnu Temple
town_description: Bishnupur is the headquarters town of Bishnupur district, about 27 km southwest of Imphal on the Tiddim road, on the western edge of the Imphal Valley near Loktak Lake. Once called Lamangdong, it took its present name from its 15th-century Vishnu temple, marking the first arrival of Vaishnavism in Manipur. The town is also known for stoneware, handloom weaving and local produce such as yongchak (tree beans) and hill oranges.
